reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

posts.text:
Very proud to pass the gavel for the Bagel Caucus to my good friend and New York bagel aficionado, @MicahLasher. 

While Micah might choose his local Barney Greengrass over my Russ and Daughters, a NY bagel is a NY bagel and I’m confident Micah will do an outstanding job of https://t.co/pxhpMbfYXS

Tomorrow is election day!

Make a plan, know your rights, and get out to VOTE. ⬇️
https://t.co/nXvB66m9Z6

I made another visit to the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn, a criminal jail that is being used to hold an increasing number of immigrants in the same conditions as criminal defendants even though the vast majority of them have never committed a crime.

I’m pleased that our persistent oversight has improved conditions somewhat, but the indefinite detention is simply unacceptable. 

I was able to receive an update on Oscar Belgal, who was shot by ICE a couple of weeks ago and is being held in the MDC, and we will continue to monitor his medical care.

I will continue to conduct oversight of @DHSgov and ensure they are held accountable for the safety of all New Yorkers.

During the 119th Congress, we defeated nearly all anti-LGBTQ+ provisions pushed by MAGA Republicans. 

I am proud to have earned a 100% rating on Human Rights Campaign’s congressional scorecard and look forward to continuing to defend LGBTQ+ freedoms. https://t.co/tcJYJYwzfr

topics.topic: Civil Rights and Liberties, Minority Issues

posts.text:
As Republicans implement their devastating cuts to SNAP, we need to be sure that those who still receive benefits actually get them.

That’s why Congress must pass my bipartisan Enhanced Cybersecurity for SNAP Act to provide federal funding to upgrade to chip-enabled EBT cards nationwide and prevent rampant SNAP fraud that is making too many people go hungry.

Once again, @DHSgov cites statistics that they refuse to verify or publicize for scrutiny.  I have repeatedly asked for further information on this data – including in the letter dated September 1st linked below – and they refuse to respond.

If these numbers are accurate, DHS should have no problem giving me the underlying information. The fact that they continue to refuse to do so seriously undermines their credibility.

https://t.co/UIFGbvaSDS

.@DHSgov officials have repeatedly denied that it has monitored protestors using a database that includes American citizens, including under oath in front of the Homeland Security Committee. In newly unsealed court filings, DHS has admitted that they have been lying all along. In fact, they have been using a Palantir database to track and intimidate Americans who have done nothing other than exercise their First Amendment rights.  

Those officials who testified falsely must be investigated for making false statements to Congress when the Democrats take over the majority.  

Congress should pass my DHS Surveillance Technology Moratorium Act of 2026, which would enact a moratorium on surveillance technology related contracts overseen by DHS, and would force a public audit by the Inspector General.  

Americans deserve to know exactly how Trump's DHS uses these tools to fuel ICE’s campaign of violence.
https://t.co/FNoAfIZNlL

posts.text:
Some rare positive news from this week’s visit to 26 Federal Plaza: zero detainees on the 10th floor and full due process and public access to the virtual courtrooms on the 3rd floor.

We raised the alarm when ICE denied me access to the virtual courtrooms (which should be under DOJ jurisdiction), and thankfully that oversight and accountability effort resulted in the removal of ICE altogether on that floor. 

Congressional oversight works. I will continue to show up and hold @DHSgov accountable.

A lot of words here but none that indicate a single reason for the ICE agent to have pulled the trigger. If previously committing a felony justified getting shot for no other reason, we would no longer live in a democracy based on the rule of law. This statement all but admits that there was no absolutely no legitimate reason to shoot.

ICE has hired thousands of unqualified, unvetted, untrained new agents, and this is yet another example of how this administration is breaking the law. 

The United States Attorney must immediately investigate this as a potential crime committed well outside the duties and responsibilities of the agent. There must be accountability.

This weekend, we hosted a Wellness Resource Fair in the district, working alongside various government agencies and community organizations to support and engage with residents of the Lower East Side.

We are grateful to every group that helped make this possible, and to all of our constituents who stopped by!

Outdated Medicaid restrictions on long-term mental health care have left too many Americans in crisis without access to treatment, and we have seen the devastating impact in New York City and around the country.

To accompany my Michelle Go Act and the Strengthening Medicaid for Serious Mental Illness Act, I am introducing the bipartisan IMD CARE Act, which would allow states to expand their mental health services and help get Americans out of the never-ending cycle of hospitals, jail, and the streets.

Boosting mental health and substance abuse treatment would have a dramatic impact on reducing crime, homelessness, and giving everyone the opportunity to succeed.
https://t.co/TscRgG6xm7

Donald Trump has used taxpayer dollars to bankroll his own personal political ads. This is a blatant misuse of Americans’ hard-earned money, and it is deceptive and misleading.

I am joining my fellow @HomelandDems on a letter demanding answers from DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin.

Unaccompanied minors — immigrant children as young as two years old — are being brought before an immigration judge and expected to adequately represent themselves. 

This year, the Trump administration allowed a contract with the Acacia Center for Justice to lapse, leaving a vacuum where the center once provided legal counsel to over 20,000 kids. 

In addition to being plainly negligent, these children are being denied due process under the Constitution of the United States of America. I have been a voice on this issue for as long as I have served in Congress, but recent events have shown unprecedented levels of cruelty by this administration that must stop once and for all.
https://t.co/vy4NrWZfvo

Why does @DHSgov continue to bar me from new rooms where immigrants are sent to have virtual hearings even though they are appearing in person, as instructed?

What are they hiding by unlawfully preventing me from conducting my congressional oversight duties?

I will keep coming back until they give me answers and let me observe their end-run around the normal legal process.

During my time in office, I have been privileged to be able to deliver a total of $15,464,700 in Community Project Funding Awards to 11 different @NYCHA  developments in the district. 

These funds support NYCHA projects improving community safety features that are crucial to the health and wellbeing of its residents. I would like to extend my gratitude to the resident leaders whose advocacy helped many of these projects come to fruition, as well as NYCHA CEO Lisa Bova-Hiatt for her leadership and commitment to the welfare of over half a million New Yorkers whom NYCHA serves.

I’m back at the 26 Federal Plaza ICE Facility, where I’ve just conducted my weekly oversight visit. Once again, immigrants are being deported to a “third country” — a foreign nation that is not their home country where they likely have no connections, family or safeguards. This group has orders that prevent them from being sent back to their home countries so this is a concerning circumvention of the law.

As rumored last week, we discovered that @DHSgov has indeed started conducting virtual immigration hearings out of this facility. During this visit, I was denied my congressional right to conduct oversight of those courtrooms, which further begs the question: What is DHS hiding?

I will continue coming back and demanding answers. As always, if you or someone you know needs assistance, my office is available to help.
https://t.co/tejX5avFO5

Today marks the solemn 25th anniversary of the September 11th attacks. 

It gives us an opportunity to mourn the thousands we lost that day, and the thousands more taken by 9/11 related illnesses. It’s a day to remember the heroes who rushed towards the towers in true New York fashion, and the victims’ families, survivors, and neighbors who still suffer from that day. 

As we reflect on 9/11’s traumatic impact on the city, let’s also remember the unity and resilience that New Yorkers showed. That was the very best of New York and it shows what we can be.

We must never forget that day, and we must also never forget our potential as a city, a country, and as Americans.

Gutted by the tragic accident on Canal St. where one pedestrian was killed and two more were injured by a truck. My office is in contact with the NYPD as we try to learn more.

I am once again calling on @NYC_DOT to address Canal Street to prioritize pedestrian safety.

Thank you @NYCGothamHealth and @NYCHealthSystem for having me today, as we commemorated the dreadful attack on 9/11 but celebrated the incredible resilience and hard work of the medical community in the 25 years since. 

Now that the City has finally relented and released dozens of boxes of documents from the immediate aftermath of the attacks, it is my hope that the expertise of the terrific doctors at Health and Hospitals can use that information to help the tens of thousands suffering from 9/11-related illnesses.

My weekly oversight visit at the 26 Federal Plaza ICE facility was again consistent with its return to its prior use as a processing center with only 3 detainees there. 

But we are monitoring troubling rumors that @DHSgov is going to start conducting virtual hearings to potentially get around an order prohibiting courthouse arrests. This would be an outrageous violation of a court order, and I strongly advise DHS to abandon this plan.

School is back after a nice, long New York summer. 

It was a pleasure to greet parents and kids on the first day of school at PS 89 with District 1 Superintendent Kelly McGuire. 

I wish all 900,000+ NYC public school students a great year. https://t.co/H3ogPYigb5

Tomorrow marks 25 years since the September 11th attacks. I am proud to lead a resolution, joined by over 200 of my colleagues, that commemorates the thousands of lives lost, reaffirms our obligation to the survivors and first responders who continue to suffer from 9/11 related illnesses, and recognizes the importance of teaching future generations the history and lessons of September 11th. We must never forget.
https://t.co/quwtpyrZRn

Today, I presented @BrooklynDA with a $354,000 check for their Support Outreach and Assistance Response (SOAR) program that provides immediate assistance to victims and their families.

When you or a loved one is the victim of a violent crime, SOAR won't hesitate to help. They’ll connect you with relocation services, trauma care, or victims' rights experts. I'm proud to have secured funding for this program, which will support Brooklyn residents through extraordinarily difficult times.

Honored to join @GovKathyHochul and the @PANYNJ today at the dedication of a powerful new memorial to the Port Authority employees who lost their lives in the World Trade Center attacks of 1993 and 2001.

Their courage and sacrifice will never be forgotten. This memorial ensures their legacy endures.

I’m proud to have joined with my colleagues Rep. Nadler, Speaker Menin, and Councilmember Brewer to pressure City Hall release of these files, and I applaud the Mayor for taking this long-overdue step. 

These documents confirm what we’ve known for a long time: the air at Ground Zero was unsafe to breathe, and those in power ignored the danger. 

Now the survivors, first responders, and victims’ families can begin to find closure, and hopefully the World Trade Center Health Program — which we were recently able to fully fund — can learn more about what has caused so many 9/11-related illnesses.

Honoring our commitment to Never Forget requires that we continue to fight for these communities every day.
https://t.co/7PbQo5HaYl

I have joined my colleagues @Sen_Gounardes @MMitaynes and @CMAlexaAviles in urging @NYC_DOT to move forward with a 3rd Ave street safety redesign. Sunset Park can no longer wait for safety improvements, especially not at the risk of losing yet another life.

My office and @CMSusanZhuang are working with the Zheng family to provide support to her loved ones in this horrible time of loss.
Deadline to apply for Summer EBT is September 8th. Apply now. https://t.co/zdy5VIs9SV

This weekend, Jiayi Zheng was killed by a speeding vehicle on 3rd Ave in Sunset Park. My office is aware of an ongoing investigation into this incident, and my thoughts are with the victims family.

Tragedies on this stretch of 3rd Ave are all too common, which is exactly why I have been calling for the @NYC_DOT to redesign this corridor to protect pedestrians and cyclists. The city must act now to prevent further loss of life.
